precepts.text: If you choose to use the sinful kingdom for America, let me give you the precept. The great city is Babylon the great, which spiritually, that's the key word you want to highlight, is called Sodom and Egypt: a spiritual Sodom, a spiritual Egypt. Where also our Lord was crucified: Christ was crucified in Jerusalem, so what is it saying? America is a spiritual Jerusalem. Just like they hated Christ in real Jerusalem, they hate the true Christ and his teachings here as well.
precepts.point: Verse 11 is where we wanted to get to: in that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen. Notice the chronology: Israel destroyed in verse 8, sifted and scattered in verse 9, the sinners die, now verse 11. He's already letting us know God's plan, his purpose. Why? Because we are predestined; because he foreknew us from before the foundation of the earth. That is fallen: what happened? The 12 tribes were split into two kingdoms. And I will build it as in the days of old: he said, I'm going to rebuild this whole thing as in the days of old.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Amos says, “Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth”. In Amos he calls us, wicked Israel, the sinful kingdom. But if you choose to use the sinful kingdom for America, as brothers do, here is the precept: “And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.”

The great city is Babylon the great. “Spiritually” is the key word to highlight: it is called Sodom and Egypt, a spiritual Sodom and a spiritual Egypt.

“Where also our Lord was crucified.” Christ was crucified in Jerusalem, so what is it saying? America is a spiritual Jerusalem. Just as they hated Christ in the real Jerusalem, they hate the true Christ and his teachings here as well.

Either way the order of Amos stands. The sinful kingdom is destroyed, “saving that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob”: not all the Israelites are wiped out. We are sifted among all nations, yet the least of us is not lost. The sinners who say the evil shall not overtake them, just like Christianity saying we good in White Jesus name, die by the sword. And then, “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen”, the twelve tribes that were split into two kingdoms, “and I will build it as in the days of old”. He is already letting us know his plan, because we are predestined, foreknown from before the foundation of the earth.

precepts.text: Therefore will he give them up, until the time that she which travaileth hath brought forth: until Israel brought forth. Then the remnant of Christ's brethren shall return unto the children of Israel. Why? Because we fell. Now he's raising us up as in the days of old. We're coming back to who we are.
precepts.point: In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Amos says, “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old.” Why does it have to be raised up? Because we fell.

Micah shows the order of it: “Therefore will he give them up, until the time that she which travaileth hath brought forth.” God gave Israel up until the woman in travail, Israel, brought forth. “then the remnant of his brethren shall return unto the children of Israel.” Then the remnant of Christ's brethren returns to the children of Israel.

That is the tabernacle of David being raised. We were given up and we fell, and now he is raising us up as in the days of old. We are coming back to who we are.

precepts.text: The children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim: little images we made of family members. Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord their God, and David their king, and shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days. So in these latter days, David's going to be here. Who he is, we don't know.
precepts.point: In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Amos says the tabernacle of David is fallen. Hosea tells how long it lies fallen: “For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim.” Teraphim are the little images we made of family members. Many days with none of it: no king, no prince, no priesthood.

“Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord their God, and David their king; and shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days.”

So in these latter days, David is going to be here. Who he is, we don't know. But the children of Israel who have gone so long without a king will return and seek the Lord their God and David their king, and that is the tabernacle of David raised up and built as in the days of old.

precepts.text: Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock: this is Christ. Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh stir up thy strength, and come and save us. Turn us again: turn us again to your laws, turn us again to our identity, our nationality, and we shall be saved.
precepts.point: In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Amos says, “I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old.” Asaph cries out for that raising: “Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock; thou that dwellest between the cherubims, shine forth.” The Shepherd of Israel is Christ.

“Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh stir up thy strength, and come and save us.” The tribes cry for him to stir up his strength and save them.

“Turn us again, O God, and cause thy face to shine; and we shall be saved.” Turn us again to your laws; turn us again to our identity, our nationality, and we shall be saved.

That is how the fallen tabernacle of David is rebuilt: the Shepherd of Israel turns the tribes back to his law and back to who they are, and closes up the breaches as in the days of old.

precepts.text: This is what James and Peter were quoting: I will raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; that they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name: those that call themselves Jewish, and those that call themselves Christian. Christian is a Greek word meaning anointed ones, and we are the anointed ones.
precepts.point: Cornelius was a centurion of the Italian band, a devout man that feared God with all his house. Where was he from? Caesarea. On the map, Caesarea sits right above Samaria: that's Manasseh's land. Cornelius was northern kingdom, not a Gentile of the nations. Do some research; do some study.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
James in Acts 15 was quoting the prophet Amos. This is what James and Peter were quoting: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof”. He is going to bring back the southern kingdom with the northern kingdom.

“And I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old”: as in the days of old, when the twelve tribes were one.

“That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name”. The heathen called by his name are those that call themselves Jewish and those that call themselves Christian. Christian is a Greek word that means anointed ones. They are not the anointed ones. We are.

So Cornelius and his house being accepted was the word of Amos coming to pass: the breach between the kingdoms being closed up, the tabernacle of David raised, and Israel set to possess the remnant of Edom, “saith the Lord that doeth this.”

precepts.text: God has another land his eyes are upon for a different reason: behold, the eyes of the Lord are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth. America is a sinful kingdom. Saving that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob: Jacob is the father of the twelve tribes. I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, because we were scattered into all nations; the sifting is a teaching process. All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, which say, The evil shall not overtake nor prevent us: that's what America, aka Egypt, has convinced you to believe, that nothing can happen to you here because Donald Trump talks tough about the strongest military and the Strait of Hormuz.
precepts.point: A land which the Lord thy God careth for: the eyes of the Lord thy God are always upon it.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 11:12 says the land God gives is “A land which the Lord thy God careth for: the eyes of the Lord thy God are always upon it”. God has his eyes upon a specific place for us. But there is another land his eyes are upon for a different reason.

“Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth”. America is a sinful kingdom, and God is looking at America to destroy it. “saving that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, saith the Lord.” Jacob is the father of the twelve tribes of Israel.

“For, lo, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, like as corn is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth.” We were scattered into all nations in slavery and captivity, so he will sift us out of every place we went. The sifting is a teaching process: our people have been trained after the ways of their colonizers, their oppressors and enslavers, and now they must be trained in the word of God to establish the house of Israel.

“All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, which say, The evil shall not overtake nor prevent us.” Those are our people who are rebellious to what God has to say and want to do things their own way. That is what America, aka Egypt, has convinced you to believe: nothing can happen to you here. You hear Donald Trump saying we have the strongest military, no one can stop us, open the Strait of Hormuz or I will blow you back to kingdom come. Stop believing you cannot be touched because this man talks tough and proud. America's kingdom is temporary; the strength that lasts comes from keeping God's commandments.

precepts.text: Flee out of the midst of Babylon and deliver every man his soul. Physically, the day may come to move to another land or city to keep the gospel moving; spiritually, flee the ways of the beast now. Deliver the real you under the sinful flesh, and do not be like Lot's wife.
precepts.point: All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, which say the evil shall not overtake nor prevent us. Some of you carry that spirit: I am an Israelite, the Lord will give me mercy. If you fall, get back up immediately, because that mindset has this future.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
Amos says, “All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, which say, The evil shall not overtake nor prevent us.” That is what God said is going to happen, and there is nothing you can do to delay or undo it. So we have to come out of the beast; we have to come out of that mentality. Jeremiah says, “Flee out of the midst of Babylon, and deliver every man his soul”.

Flee out of Babylon can be physical. That day may come when we have to go to different lands: some of us will be exiles, some will be deported, and sometimes you may have to go to the next city or somewhere else to keep this gospel moving. But it is also spiritual: we have to flee out of the ways of the beast now.

“Deliver every man his soul”: the soul is the real you, underneath this sinful flesh, and the Lord is telling us to deliver it. That means letting go of the things we are accustomed to here. We cannot be like Lot's wife, who looked back and became a part of the Lord's sacrifice.

The Lord is giving us the place, the time and the opportunity to get ourselves right, but the day of the Lord is approaching regardless. Some carry the spirit of those who say the evil shall not overtake them: I am an Israelite, I don't have to worry, the Lord will give me mercy. We cannot roll in that mentality. If you fall, get back up immediately, because that mindset has this future. We are in the midst of a spiritual war, and we have to meditate on these things constantly, get our minds right and stay steadfast until the end.

precepts.text: Arise, O Lord, disappoint him, cast him down; deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword. God wields the wicked as his sword, and the wicked today is the United States. We do not bug out over what we see; we understand why it is happening and what we have to do.
precepts.point: They send drones that cost fifteen to twenty thousand dollars and the other side fires interceptors that cost a million or more to knock them down. You see how they will not be able to keep up, and how God put all this in these leaders.

note.label: Wars Are Here: Seek Good Not Evil

precepts.why:
Amos says, “And though they go into captivity before their enemies, thence will I command the sword, and it shall slay them”. Who is the sword? The wicked at the time. David shows it: “Arise, O Lord, disappoint him, cast him down: deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword”, and he goes on, “From men which are thy hand, O Lord”.

God wields the wicked as his sword. The wicked today is the United States. He is going to use them to bring in all these wars you are seeing, and we have to get right.

That is why we can't bug out or get caught up in everything going on. Nobody wants to see Arab children losing limbs; nobody wants to see destruction. But we understand why it is happening, and we understand what we have to do, so that when the final war comes, he that endureth to the end shall be saved. That is what we want: deliverance.

So it was with us. The twelve tribes went into captivity after captivity before our enemies, because God allowed every bit of it. He commanded the sword and it slew us, and he set his eyes upon us “for evil, and not for good”, because we did not keep the commandments. The Iranians don't get a pass; they had us in captivity too, as did the princes of Ishmael. There is slavery happening right now in parts of Africa, and it is not Black Americans or Israelites running it, but Arabs and Caucasians with financial power. Wars are here: seek good and not evil.

precepts.text: Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure. This is our power: the Most High planned every war, including the third world war, from the time of Adam. He is behind the Israelis in the US government and behind Iran's twenty years of tunnels and munitions. Chattel slavery, Jim Crow, and civil rights were his pleasure too; we had to learn the lesson.
precepts.point: They send drones that cost fifteen to twenty thousand dollars and the other side fires interceptors that cost a million or more to knock them down. You see how they will not be able to keep up, and how God put all this in these leaders.

note.label: Wars Are Here: Seek Good Not Evil

precepts.why:
Amos says “the Lord God of hosts is he that toucheth the land”. When Iran is being touched right now, and Israel, the Lord is involved in all of it; by his counsel the land gets touched. Isaiah shows that counsel: “Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done”.

This is the power we have: understanding that the Most High God from the very beginning planned every war, including the third world war to come. Ancient times means way back when Adam and Eve walked. From then he declared it. As his sons and daughters, the Israelites, we have to know our Father has this covered and his Son is coming back. Right now we have to rehearse the righteous acts and get right.

That is how we can make the bold statement that God is behind the Israelis doing what they do in the US government, and behind the Iranians spending twenty years building huge, elaborate tunnel systems and storing munitions and advanced rocketry. All of it was set up from ancient times. They send drones that cost fifteen to twenty thousand dollars, and the other side fires interceptor missiles that cost a million or more to take them out. You see how they will not be able to keep up. God put all that in these leaders.

“My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure”. It was his pleasure when we went into chattel slavery, through Jim Crow and through civil rights. We had to learn the lesson.

Jeremiah shows the same counsel: “Therefore hear ye the counsel of the Lord, that he hath taken against Babylon”. “Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out”: Israel, the least of Esau's flock, draws the United States out into the Middle East, and “At the noise of the taking of Babylon the earth is moved”. Amos lived way before anything could melt the land. Today thermonuclear ICBMs can, and it is all by his counsel.

precepts.text: In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof, and raise up his ruins, and build it as in the days of old, that they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen which are called by my name. The twelve tribes possess Edom and the heathen called by his name; other nations cannot be part of our reconciliation, restoration, or reparation.
precepts.point: Sin is the transgression of the law, 1 John 3:4. Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law: those under the law break it and are under sin, and both Jews and Gentiles under sin means both under the law, which the other nations never were. That every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God, the world that received God's commandments under Moses. Therefore by the deeds of the law, sacrifice, there shall no flesh be justified in his sight, for we are justified by Christ's blood; for by the law is the knowledge of sin, because to acknowledge a sin, willful or ignorant, you had to bring an animal.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
Acts 15 quotes the prophet Amos: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof”. The breaches are the tear, the split, like the breach “great like the sea” in Lamentations. Remember, the root word of reparations is to repair.

“And I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old”. This is the restoring of Israel, both kingdoms that Paul proved “are all under sin” in Romans 3, repaired and raised up as in the days of old.

Then: “That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name, saith the Lord that doeth this.” That they, all twelve tribes, may possess the remnant of Edom and of the heathen called by his name.

So you see, other nations cannot be involved in our reconciliation, our restoration or our reparation. The ones called by his name, the Christians and the Jews, are not the tabernacle being raised; they are what Israel possesses once it is raised. This goes back to the classes before on Romans 11 and Acts 10.

precepts.text: I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth.
precepts.point: Let both grow together until the harvest; God will reveal who is Israel.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
In the parable, “while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat”. A mixing happened: bad seed sown in among the good seed. “An enemy hath done this.” It was done on purpose. For the Northern Kingdom tribes in this hemisphere, that was the whitening the Spaniards practiced: marrying to lighter skin to better the race, with a whole caste system of names for every kind of mixing. They found the tribes, and since they could not kill us all outright, they tried to pollute the royal seed. But however watered down the daughter is, one man with the seed of an Israelite brings it back.

The servants asked, should we gather up the tares? “Nay; lest while ye gather up the tares, ye root up also the wheat with them. Let both grow together until the harvest”. It is not for us to determine, because of the way this went down; we do not know who is and who is not. At the harvest the angels will know who is Israel.

Amos proves it: “For, lo, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all nations”. Why among all nations? Because through the whitening, the mixing and the captivities, God himself has to be the one to sift us. “Like as corn is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth.” It will be determined who is who. Even Adam had to walk through a gate; you do not have twelve gates with twelve names and think somebody is going to sneak through. God said he will do it. My sheep hear my voice, and you know them by their works.

“All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, which say, The evil shall not overtake nor prevent us.” He is going to kill a lot of them, before, during and even some after. So we narrow down where our people gather and go to the chief places of concourse, not to where the Edomites are, and give the word; and let God do the separating.

precepts.text: In that day God raises up the tabernacle of David that is fallen.
precepts.point: The residue of men seek after the Lord in servitude, and the Gentiles called by his name are those who call themselves Jews and Christians.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
Isaiah spoke of “the day that the Lord bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.” What does it mean to bind up the breach of his people? Acts 15 answers it. “Simeon hath declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name. And to this agree the words of the prophets”: “After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down”. That is bringing back the twelve tribes of Israel.

James was quoting Amos: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof”. Closing up the breaches is the binding up of the breach in Isaiah 30: when he gathers the twelve tribes of Israel back again. Right now the tabernacle is still fallen; we are trying to gather ourselves together. “and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old”.

“That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name”. Possess means own. We are going to own the remnant of Edom and all the nations. The heathen called by his name are those who call themselves Jews and Christians. Jew comes from Judah, which means praise of God, so Amalek is saying they are the praise of God, and they're not. Christian means anointed ones, calling themselves God's anointed. All of them that call themselves by those names, we are going to possess, “saith the Lord that doeth this”: he is going to make sure that thing is done.

precepts.text: It is he that buildeth his stories in the heaven.
precepts.point: The heavens are built in stories, like the three stories of the temple and the ark.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“It is he that buildeth his stories in the heaven”. What are the stories he builds in the heaven? The first layer, the second layer and the third layer: the sky of this earth, space, and paradise. Paul calls it the third heaven. Those are the stories, three different layers.

Above them is the Father, at the very top, the holy of holies. Where he is, is infinite; it is called eternity. That is why we call him the Majesty on high. He is the highest, and the Most High, the Highest, is one of the few titles Christ does not have. That title is his Father's. They are not the same person.

Read on: “and hath founded his troop in the earth”. The troop is us. “he that calleth for the waters of the sea, and poureth them out upon the face of the earth: The Lord is his name.” From there, back to Genesis 1:6: “Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters”. The waters are space, and the firmament was made in the midst of space. Atmosphere means vapor sphere, and vapor means water: layers of water that circle the earth and protect it from the sun. So there are levels of heaven over the earth, then space, then paradise, with levels there too. As above, so below. Paradise was created on the second day, when God made the firmament and called it heaven.

precepts.text: In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen.
precepts.point: The nations shall bring Israel to its place and serve as servants and handmaids.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
The Lord “will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land.” Judah shall live on the sea coast, and it gets better: “For God will save Zion, and will build the cities of Judah: that they may dwell there, and have it in possession.” And Amos: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old.” The tabernacle of David is the twelve tribes, built again as in the days of old.

“That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name.” There are people calling themselves Jewish today, and Jew comes from Judah, praise of Yahawah; they are not the praise of Yahawah. And people calling themselves Christians, the anointed ones; they are not the anointed ones.

“And I will bring again the captivity of my people of Israel, and they shall build the waste cities, and inhabit them.” There are waste cities all over there, and after Armageddon there will be more. And we will have servants: that is the strangers joined to the house of Jacob, the heathen round about us as bondmen and bondmaids, when that law goes back in full effect.

“And I will plant them upon their land, and they shall no more be pulled up out of their land which I have given them, saith the Lord thy God.” That is Isaiah 14:1 fulfilled: set in their own land, never pulled out again.

precepts.text: The tabernacle of David is raised up, that they may possess the remnant of Edom and of all the heathen.
precepts.point: In thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed: those nations are the nations of Israel, the twelve tribes.

note.label: Genesis 22: The Offering of Isaac

precepts.why:
“Thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies.” That is part of the covenant, and Amos shows who possesses whom: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old: That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name, saith the Lord that doeth this.”

The seed of Jacob possesses the remnant of Edom and of all the heathen. That is why all nations cannot be inside this covenant: the covenant has Israel possessing their enemies. So “in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed” speaks of the nations of Israel, the twelve tribes.

precepts.text: In that day the Most High raises up the fallen tabernacle of David so that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the heathen called by his name.
precepts.point: The Most High chooses Israel's inheritance for them; it will not be up to you to say you do not want to rule the nations. The spirit will be put on you and you will be kings, your wives goddesses and queens, your sons princes, your daughters princesses, ruling the whole planet in righteousness.

note.label: Psalm 47: God the Great King Over All the Earth

precepts.why:
“He shall subdue the people under us, and the nations under our feet. He shall choose our inheritance for us”. Amos tells when: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old: That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name, saith the Lord that doeth this.”

The fallen tabernacle of David is raised up so that Israel may possess the remnant of Edom and all the heathen called by his name. That is the inheritance chosen for us, the excellency of Jacob whom he loved; and it is the Lord that doeth this, not us choosing whether we want it.

precepts.text: In that day He will raise up the fallen tabernacle of David, close up the breaches, and build it as in the days of old.
precepts.point: It shall be to Him a name of joy, a praise, and an honor before all nations, who will fear and tremble at the goodness He procures, for the nations know this is true and are struck when they see us carry ourselves as sons and daughters of the covenant.

note.label: Jeremiah 33: The Branch of Righteousness and the Covenant of Day and Night

precepts.why:
The Lord will cause the captivity of Judah and the captivity of Israel to return, “and will build them, as at the first.” Amos speaks of that building: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old”.

In that day he raises up the fallen tabernacle of David, closes up the breaches, and builds it as in the days of old, which is building them as at the first. It has not yet been fulfilled; there is still much violence in Israel and against us, and the abundance of peace and truth is still to be revealed. When it is, it will be a name of joy, a praise and an honour before all the nations of the earth.
